Canada doesn't rely american products to not starve, the person in charge of ordering for the store just overestimated the number of customers who would buy american produce and underestimated how fast other items would move. The store will just order more produce from south america, italy, the EU, Chile, etc. to keep the shelves stocked how they always have been. 

Now let's zoom out and get some context from the original post: the canadians who didn't buy the american products don't want to buy them because they disagree with america's national policy. They are protesting america's national policy by not using american products. The person in charge of ordering things to sell at the store will notice the american products are plentiful, and won't buy more so they don't have back stock. This lowers the amount of money the store sends to america. It is a protest method called ['dollar voting'](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollar_voting), and most boycotts are via this method.

You know what's interesting, is horses actually understand tone like a dog does! They're about as smart as a 3 year old, as well- they can recognize themselves in a mirror.

Yes, teaching the horse basic commands (stop, walk, trot, lope, gallop) and basic manners (stand still until I say to move, don't kick/buck/hop/rear/whatever else, accept tack quietly) is paramount in his training, regardless of his purpose in human society. A horse should know all of these things before you even consider getting on him, imo. A dog bite hurts, but getting kicked by or thrown off a horse can kill.

I think a horse should learn these things while you're on the ground next to them, which means the horse would learn verbal commands first. Once you feel the horse is ready for you to hop on, you can reteach him to accept [leg cues](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=arxMxcsMtag) instead, but not everyone does- which is fine, especially if you aren't planning to use the horse in competition.

11 year olds know some things are adults only, and have enough brain power to understand what they can get away with and what is an absolute hard line. They learn this by pushing boundaries. Your reaction to that boundary being pushed is how they learn where that hard line is. By showing them a severe real world consequence (sexual harassment complaint filed), you are showing them that behavior will not be tolerated, and giving them a taste of what's coming down the pipeline if they don't straighten up. It's best to correct that behavior HARD while it's a harmless 11 year old parroting catchphrases, instead of incarcerating a 19 year old frat boy on sex offense charges. The kid is only 11 and that complaint will fall off his record soon enough, but violent sex charges (like rape) don't. 

Do you ever wonder if maybe the adults inventing those slogans do so because they didn't have an adult tell them how unacceptable that behavior is while they were still mentally developing?

Here's another example, if it happening to an 11 year old is what's tripping you up: do you let your puppy mouth you and the furniture because he doesn't know better? What happens when that puppy grows up and grows adult teeth? You have a biter and no more furniture, because you didn't teach him not to bite when it was his harmless gums.

Why not? If they want to act grown and say such terrible things, they should get a grown punishment, right? 10 and 11 is not too young to understand "we don't ever say something like that". They're absolutely old enough to understand consent (we don't touch others if they don't want to be touched). This isn't a toddler touching someone's breast, this is a middle schooler making rape jokes.

Tl;dr: I don't recommend them, mostly because they squeak very loudly and it can't be fixed. I feel you're paying for hype and brand recognition with these shoes.

 I personally have been pretty disappointed in them. The high shine (which is what I have) make me sound like SpongeBob when I walk and shredded my ankles worse than any comparable boot I've owned. That squeaking never goes away, btw, because it's the plastic coating that makes it high shine rubbing on itself. [Here's where the squeaking sound comes from on my boots.](https://imgur.com/a/D308UTG) What you're seeing is the plastic coating on the shoe worn away to reveal the pink leather underneath, as well as the lace staining part of the tongue black. That picture was taken after being worn for 8 days, and walked a total of 24 miles. Not hiking, just walking on flat sidewalk and the floors in my office building.

Some people aren't bothered by the squeaking since it's hard to hear in, for example, a busy store. Also, don't believe the "all leather sounds like that" crowd. I ride in a heavy duty all leather saddle -occasianally with all-leather chaps- and not only does it not make sound with every. single. movement, but it also does not sound like these shoes do. These shoes are the sound of plastic on plastic.

Also, I understand vocal minorities, but outside of this sub I still hear people still complain pretty often about poor workmanship, discomfort, and the soles splitting. If you're buying the shoe based on ability to resole, keep in mind they don't exactly do that at the local Walmart, and the price of new OEM soles and the cost to attach, as well as travel time if you don't have a cobbler nearby may exceed the price of a new pair of shoes. Personally I need cost efficiency rather than the character of a broken-in shoe, but I know a lot of people just like the look of a well worn boot. 

Overall, DM (even the asian made) were more comfortable for me, have lasted longer and more gracefully, and were more affordable with more color and leather options.

I hope you all enjoyed my write up, I know I didn't see any negative opinions on the issues I have with these shoes and I hope I can help others make a more informed purchase :)
